newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria delays building nuclear waste storage.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria delays building nuclear waste storage.

text.p: Bulgaria, which gets half of its electricity from nuclear power, faces a delay in building a new storage facility for radioactive nuclear waste due to a lack of money, a senior official said on Monday.

Kiril Nikolov, acting chairman of the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, said 86 million levs, transfered to them by the environmental ministry, had been blocked at the Economic Bank, which has been recently put under special supervision.
Two weeks ago Bulgaria placed nine banks under special supervision in a bid to stabilise its crambling financial system and depositors can not withdraw their money from them.
"Now we have difficulties with funding the construction but we also rely on another six million Ecus from the (European Union's) Phare programme," Nikolov told reporters.
Nikolov said the Kozloduy's temporary storages for the spent fuel of the two 1,000-megawatt reactors, were almost full.
"Their capacity allows to store (spent) fuel for another 2-3 years," Nikolov said.
In the past, the Soviet Union reprocessed and disposed of spent fuel from Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant free of charge under a bilateral agreement.
The accord expired in 1990 and the spent fuel has since been left unprocessed in a temporary storage in Bulgaria.
Moscow also adopted a 1992 law on environmental protection banning the shipment of nuclear waste to its territory.
Apart from the low and intermediate level waste storage, Bulgaria plans to build a storage facility for highly radioactive waste and last February called a tender for the project.
The facility, which will be built at the site of the Kozloduy plant, will store waste for up to 50 years.
Officials have said the first of the three stages of the construction of the new facility for dry storing of the waste should be completed by 1999 and ensure the storage of rods, totalling 5,000.
